title: GREAT LAKES SURFACE WATER TEMPERATURE
noaa_source: NOAA/GLERL CoastWatch GLSEA (Great Lakes Surface Environmental Analysis)
product_name: NOAA/GLERL CoastWatch GLSEA (Great Lakes Surface Environmental Analysis)
variable: lake surface water temperature (satellite-derived AVHRR/VIIRS composite)
spatial_resolution_rendered: 1800x1175 canvas over lon [-93.0,-73.5], lat [40.5,49.5] (mean-value binning, no upsampling of source precision)
missing_data_treatment: land code 255.0 and -9999/no-data rendered fully transparent; never interpolated.
shoreline_mask: assets/great_lakes_watermask.png — shared NOAA medium-resolution shoreline water mask (nautical-chart compilation, mean-high-water datum; snapped + polygonized once, full vertex precision, antialiased). Overlay alpha is multiplied by this mask and edge RGB is bled into transparent pixels (anti-fringe for bilinear clients), so every product shares one shoreline.
attribution: Data: US NOAA. This project is not endorsed by NOAA. See DATA_SOURCES.md for exact products and endpoints.
label_method: Actual °F values (e.g. 45°F) in white mono with a dark outline, free placement: data-seeded jittered candidates (positions move with the water, never a fixed grid), thermal-front cells first, spaced fill up to quota.
legend_scale_html: Surface water temperature (°F): cold 46°F (deep blue) → 55°F → warm 64°F (red). Lakewide mean this run: 54.7°F. White halo numbers are actual °F at that spot. The bar ends are recomputed every run from that day's water (1st/99th percentiles, clamped 32–86°F): blue always means the coldest water present and red the warmest, but the same color can stand for a different °F on different days — only the printed numbers are absolute.
live_doc_html:
Great Lakes Coverage legend

Legend

Surface water temperature (°F): cold 46°F (deep blue) → 55°F → warm 64°F (red). Lakewide mean this run: 54.7°F. White halo numbers are actual °F at that spot. The bar ends are recomputed every run from that day's water (1st/99th percentiles, clamped 32–86°F): blue always means the coldest water present and red the warmest, but the same color can stand for a different °F on different days — only the printed numbers are absolute.

Continental Lake Coverage legend

Legend

Surface water temperature (°F) — Continental Lake Coverage: cold 32°F (deep blue) → 57°F → warm 82°F (red). Mean this run: 51.8°F. White halo numbers are actual °F at that spot. Endpoints are recomputed every run from this coverage's own tracked inland-lake water only (MUR open-lake cells plus Great Lakes GLSEA cells; 1st/99th percentiles, clamped 32–86°F, linear mapping between them). Ocean water is excluded from this distribution, so the same color stands for a different °F than in the other coverages — only the printed numbers are absolute. Lakes below the fetch sampling, frozen lakes outside the open-lake mask state, and rivers stay transparent and are never fabricated.

Extended Oceanic Coverage legend

Legend

Surface water temperature (°F) — Extended Oceanic Coverage: cold 28°F (deep blue) → 57°F → warm 86°F (red). Mean this run: 57.6°F. White halo numbers are actual °F at that spot. Endpoints are recomputed every run from all valid water across this coverage's supported global dataset (oceans and seas from blended SST, inland lakes from MUR, Great Lakes from GLSEA; each observation counted once; 1st/99th percentiles with floor/ceil rounding; low end unclamped so polar water (~28°F) reads correctly, high end clamped 86°F; linear mapping between them). The same color stands for a different °F than in the other coverages — only the printed numbers are absolute. Unsupported or unobserved water stays transparent and is never fabricated.

This layer holds three coverages in one folder: Great Lakes Coverage (default), Continental Lake Coverage, Extended Oceanic Coverage. Check exactly one at a time (Google Earth Pro switches them exclusively; Web/app users check one box manually). Great Lakes Coverage is always the default: a fresh load or data refresh restores it (a saved project may keep your own last-used checkboxes until you toggle back). Each coverage has its own scale because its colors come from its own water — all three legends are right here, so no submenu is needed.
